title_original: How to Conceal and Reveal with Arpita Shah
editorial_title_zh: 如何通过阿尔皮塔·沙阿（Arpita Shah）的作品去隐藏与显露
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这位艺术家的作品捕捉到了他人生活根本不可知的一部分特质
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "这位艺术家的作品捕捉到了他人生活根本不可知的一部分特质", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在阿尔皮塔·沙阿（Arpita Shah）展览的入口处，摆放着一张玻璃顶的展陈桌，具有鲜明的博物馆风格，各种物品被归档、贴上标签并展出：护照（印度的）、硬币、信件、一对色彩斑斓的糖果盒（来自孟买和内罗毕）、珠子、干花、宝石、一块砖头、一堆卷曲的黑白与彩色家庭合影，以及各种年代的风景明信片和宗教圣像。正是这种展陈方式，而不是任何单个物品本身，暗示着它们的珍贵。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些是可能构成任何移民家族历史记录的便携材料（出生于印度的艺术家本人曾在沙特阿拉伯和爱尔兰之间辗转，最后定居英国）。更具体地说，它们是沙阿自身传统的纪念品，始于她的祖母（即展览标题中的娜利尼［Nalini］），她从印度搬到了肯尼亚（后来又搬了回去），不过在这里，将这些纪念品从家庭语境中剥离并纳入制度化的分类学中，在这些物品的主观价值与客观价值之间产生了一种奇妙的张力。我们能像艺术家那样珍视它们吗？你会不禁这样想。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://backend.artreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Canal-Road-from-the-series-Nalini-©-Arpita-Shah-copy-1230x984.jpg", "alt": "Canal Road from the series Nalini © Arpita Shah", "caption": "Canal Road , 2017, 59 x 42. @ the artist. Courtesy Firstsite, Colchester", "credit": "ArtReview", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这或许是一个线索，引向沙阿母系血脉（祖母、母亲、自己）的摄影考古（由艺术家创作的26幅大型、装裱并悬挂于墙上的地点和人物照片，与更多家族传家宝交织在一起），这也构成了展览本身的主体。从字面意义上讲，这是一场为非个人档案的骨架注入血肉的练习。既是为了让普通观众理解那个开场的陈列柜，也是作为艺术家本人的一种记录——当她的古吉拉特语祖母由于地理和语言的隔阂而与她渐行渐远、记忆力日渐衰退时，她试图发掘自己家族传统各个方面的尝试。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在第一批艺术作品中，我们看到了她的曾祖母纳曼达（Narmanda）被装裱起来的护照，旁边放着干九重葛花瓣（由艺术家从内罗毕昔日家族奶牛场遗址采摘）( Canal Road , 2017)，以及一张黑发女性的彩色照片，她将脸转开镜头，在一株九重葛灌木前摆姿势( Bougainvillea Mahara , 2016)。这与陈列柜中一张来自1985年的家庭照片遥相呼应，照片中艺术家的母亲站在艾哈迈达巴德的花朵前，略带自我意识地注视着我们。护照包含一张黑白照片，并对所有者的发色描述为“黑色和微白”，其子女为“无”。九重葛作为一种在英国殖民统治下从（巴西）移植到印度的植物，具有重要意义。最终，这两件相邻作品的组合唤起了一种既像修复又像重演的感觉。同时也引入了花卉供奉这一贯穿整个展览的重复主题。Nalini在梵语中意为“莲花”，这种花经常在印度教的普贾（pujas）仪式中用作神圣的供品；在这里，Nalini in Bloom (2016)展出了一张饰有莲花花瓣的档案肖像。在一个摄影三联画中，我们看到了一张娜利尼腐烂双腿的照片，一张池塘中盛开的莲花的照片，以及第三张艺术家母亲（明显更年轻）的上半身照片，优雅地将祖先的联结具象化，这朵花既是女性身体的隐喻，也是无可避免的衰败的隐喻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://backend.artreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Nalini_s-hands-from-the-series-Nalini-©-Arpita-Shah-copy-1230x984.jpg", "alt": "Nalini_s hands from the series Nalini © Arpita Shah copy", "caption": "Nalini’s Hand , 2017, photograph, 89 x 71 cm. @ the artist. Courtesy Firstsite, Colchester", "credit": "ArtReview", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在其他地方，我们看到一些照片，其中包含来自档案的肖像（我们可能会从开场陈列柜的标签中认出艺术家的母亲雷什马［Reshma］，她于1973年在艾哈迈达巴德被拍摄），这些肖像被拼贴进了一串海沫花环中( White Sands , 2017)，并与一张题为Mombasa (2017)的彩色照片中的海滩泡沫相配，或者被一只满是皱纹的老年女性的手紧紧握住( Nalini’s Hand , 2017)。或许其中最令人辛酸的是一张两个女性身体相拥的照片，照片中两人的前臂新旧皮肤相互触碰，手肘相扣( Mother’s Mother , 2018)。如果说连结与亲密是这些影像的主题（也是沙阿进行祖先研究项目的动机），值得注意的是，面孔只出现在档案影像中。在沙阿自己的照片中，头部总是背对观众或在构图中被裁剪掉，这使得她的照片既是失落的记录，也是寻回的记录。事实上，这些作品在显露的同时也隐藏了同样多的东西，正是因为它们坚持认为他人生活根本不可知，才显得格外感人。当然，也正是具体面孔的缺失，为观众提供了将自身体验投射到沙阿作品中的空间，这些作品对个人与集体历史的交汇点以及两者在（重构）身份认同中的影响进行了丰富研究。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Arpita Shah: Nalini at Firstsite, Colchester, 13 June – 4 October", "links": [{"text": "13 June – 4 October", "url": "https://firstsite.uk/event/exhibition-arpita-shah-nalini/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "From the October 2026 issue of ArtReview – get your copy .", "links": [{"text": "get your copy", "url": "https://shop.artreview.com/products/artreview-october-2026-the-philanthropy-report"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Share", "links": [{"text": "Share", "url": "https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://artreview.com/arpita-shah-nalini-firstsite-colchester-review-mark-rappolt/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Tweet", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The artist’s works capture something of the fundamental unknowability of other people’s lives"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "At the threshold of Arpita Shah’s exhibition is a glass-topped display table, recognisably of the museological variety, in which various objects are archived, labelled and displayed: passports (Indian), coins, letters, a pair of colourful confectionary tins (from Bombay and Nairobi), beads, dried flowers, gemstones, a piece of brick, a mix of curling black-and-white and colour family portraits, together with postcards of landscapes and religious icons of various vintages. It’s the mode of display rather than any of the individual objects themselves that suggests that they are valuable."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "These are the kind of portable materials that might constitute the record of any migrant’s family history (born in India, the artist herself moved between Saudi Arabia and Ireland before ending up in the UK). More particularly they are souvenirs of Shah’s own heritage, starting with her grandmother (the Nalini of the show’s title), who moved from India to Kenya (and then back again), although here the extraction of these keepsakes from a domestic context and their insertion into an institutional taxonomy creates a curious tension between the subjective and the objective values of the items. Could we value them as much as the artist does? You wonder."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://backend.artreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Canal-Road-from-the-series-Nalini-©-Arpita-Shah-copy-1230x984.jpg", "alt": "Canal Road from the series Nalini © Arpita Shah", "caption": "Canal Road , 2017, 59 x 42. @ the artist. Courtesy Firstsite, Colchester", "credit": "ArtReview"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A cue, perhaps, for the photographic archaeology (26 largescale, framed and wall-mounted photographs, by the artist, of places and people, mixed with further family heirlooms) of Shah’s matrilineal descent (grandmother, mother, self) that constitutes the main exhibition itself. An exercise, literally, in putting flesh on the bones of the impersonal archive. Both to give meaning to that opening vitrine for a general audience and as a chronicle of the artist’s own attempt to uncover aspects of her heritage as her Gujarati grandmother, distanced from the artist by both geography and language, became increasingly forgetful."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In the first artworks, we witness the framed passport of her great-grandmother Narmanda, with dried bougainvillea petals (picked by the artist from the site of what was formerly the family’s dairy farm in Nairobi) ( Canal Road , 2017) placed next to a colour photograph of a dark-haired woman, her face turned away from the lens, posing in front of a bougainvillea shrub ( Bougainvillea Mahara , 2016). It has echoes of a family photograph, from the vitrine, of the artist’s mother in front of flowers in Ahmedabad from 1985, as she looks out at us self-consciously. The passport contains a black-and-white photograph, along with the description of the owner’s hair colour as ‘black and greying’, her children ‘nil’. The bougainvillea is significant as a plant transplanted (from Brazil) to India under British colonial rule. Ultimately the pairing of the two adjacent works conjures a feeling that is part restoration, part reenactment. But also introduces the floral offering as a repeated theme throughout the show. Nalini means ‘lotus’ in Sanskrit, and the flower is often used as a sacred offering in Hindu pujas ; here Nalini in Bloom (2016) features a portrait from the archive garlanded with the flower’s petals. In one photographic triptych we encounter a photograph of Nalini’s decaying legs, another of a lotus blooming in a pond and a third of the (notably younger) upper body of the artist’s mother, elegantly concretising ancestral connectedness, the flower as a metaphor for the female body and the inevitability of decay."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://backend.artreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Nalini_s-hands-from-the-series-Nalini-©-Arpita-Shah-copy-1230x984.jpg", "alt": "Nalini_s hands from the series Nalini © Arpita Shah copy", "caption": "Nalini’s Hand , 2017, photograph, 89 x 71 cm. @ the artist. Courtesy Firstsite, Colchester", "credit": "ArtReview"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Elsewhere we see photographs featuring portraits from the archive (we might recognise the artist’s mother, Reshma, photographed in Ahmedabad in 1973, from the labels in the opening vitrine) collaged into a garland of sea spume ( White Sands , 2017) paired with the beachfront spume in a colour photograph titled Mombasa (2017), or clutched in a wrinkled, elderly female hand ( Nalini’s Hand , 2017). article_text:
The artist’s works capture something of the fundamental unknowability of other people’s lives

At the threshold of Arpita Shah’s exhibition is a glass-topped display table, recognisably of the museological variety, in which various objects are archived, labelled and displayed: passports (Indian), coins, letters, a pair of colourful confectionary tins (from Bombay and Nairobi), beads, dried flowers, gemstones, a piece of brick, a mix of curling black-and-white and colour family portraits, together with postcards of landscapes and religious icons of various vintages. It’s the mode of display rather than any of the individual objects themselves that suggests that they are valuable.

These are the kind of portable materials that might constitute the record of any migrant’s family history (born in India, the artist herself moved between Saudi Arabia and Ireland before ending up in the UK). More particularly they are souvenirs of Shah’s own heritage, starting with her grandmother (the Nalini of the show’s title), who moved from India to Kenya (and then back again), although here the extraction of these keepsakes from a domestic context and their insertion into an institutional taxonomy creates a curious tension between the subjective and the objective values of the items. Could we value them as much as the artist does? You wonder.

A cue, perhaps, for the photographic archaeology (26 largescale, framed and wall-mounted photographs, by the artist, of places and people, mixed with further family heirlooms) of Shah’s matrilineal descent (grandmother, mother, self) that constitutes the main exhibition itself. An exercise, literally, in putting flesh on the bones of the impersonal archive. Both to give meaning to that opening vitrine for a general audience and as a chronicle of the artist’s own attempt to uncover aspects of her heritage as her Gujarati grandmother, distanced from the artist by both geography and language, became increasingly forgetful.

In the first artworks, we witness the framed passport of her great-grandmother Narmanda, with dried bougainvillea petals (picked by the artist from the site of what was formerly the family’s dairy farm in Nairobi) ( Canal Road , 2017) placed next to a colour photograph of a dark-haired woman, her face turned away from the lens, posing in front of a bougainvillea shrub ( Bougainvillea Mahara , 2016). It has echoes of a family photograph, from the vitrine, of the artist’s mother in front of flowers in Ahmedabad from 1985, as she looks out at us self-consciously. The passport contains a black-and-white photograph, along with the description of the owner’s hair colour as ‘black and greying’, her children ‘nil’. The bougainvillea is significant as a plant transplanted (from Brazil) to India under British colonial rule. Ultimately the pairing of the two adjacent works conjures a feeling that is part restoration, part reenactment. But also introduces the floral offering as a repeated theme throughout the show. Nalini means ‘lotus’ in Sanskrit, and the flower is often used as a sacred offering in Hindu pujas ; here Nalini in Bloom (2016) features a portrait from the archive garlanded with the flower’s petals. In one photographic triptych we encounter a photograph of Nalini’s decaying legs, another of a lotus blooming in a pond and a third of the (notably younger) upper body of the artist’s mother, elegantly concretising ancestral connectedness, the flower as a metaphor for the female body and the inevitability of decay.

Elsewhere we see photographs featuring portraits from the archive (we might recognise the artist’s mother, Reshma, photographed in Ahmedabad in 1973, from the labels in the opening vitrine) collaged into a garland of sea spume ( White Sands , 2017) paired with the beachfront spume in a colour photograph titled Mombasa (2017), or clutched in a wrinkled, elderly female hand ( Nalini’s Hand , 2017). Perhaps most poignant of all is a photograph of two female bodies embracing in which the old skin and the young skin of the forearms of the individuals touch as their elbows interlock ( Mother’s Mother , 2018). If connection and proximity are themes of the images (and motivations for Shah’s project of ancestral research), it’s noticeable that faces only appear in images from the archive. In Shah’s own photographs heads are turned away from the viewer or cropped out of shot, making her photographs as much a record of loss as they are of recovery. Indeed, these are works that conceal as much as they appear to reveal, and are all the more moving for their insistence on the fundamental unknowability of other people’s lives. Although, of course, it is also the absence of specific faces that allows the viewer space to project their own experiences onto Shah’s works, which present a rich study of the intersections of personal and collective histories, and the effect of both in (re)constructing identity.

Arpita Shah: Nalini at Firstsite, Colchester, 13 June – 4 October

article_text:
Robert Pattinson recently told GamesRadar+ that he is looking forward to finishing production on “The Batman Part II” with Steven Soderbergh taking over principal photography from Matt Reeves , who exited production earlier this month due to a family matter.

“I am so happy he’s come on to help Matt,” Pattinson said of Soderbergh. “It’s incredibly generous of him – and he’s doing it in the loveliest way. It’s completely selfless. I think Matt had put so much work into the script, and we’re almost done. So for someone to come in and say, ‘I just want to help Matt do it; I want to do it in conjunction with him and just get it to the edit.’ And to have someone who’s as talented as Steven doing it is great.”

Popular on Variety

'Matchbox' Stars Jessica Biel and John Cena Lead New American Red Cross Pledge Drive (EXCLUSIVE)

When asked when filming would start up again, Pattinson responded: “I think they’re in production already. And I’m starting in a couple of days.”

Warner Bros. announced Oct. 5 that Reeves needed to take a step back from filming due to a family matter, but no specific reason was given for his leave nor has there been any update if “The Batman Part II” will need to shift its release date from Feb. 18, 2028.

“Production on ‘The Batman Part II’ has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” a studio rep said at the time. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.”

Reeves took to his X profile shortly after to clarify that he very much remains the director of “The Batman Part II,” explaining: “Just to be clear, I am not leaving ‘The Batman Part II.’ I am profoundly grateful to Steven for coming to my aid during this challenging time to help me finish principal photography. Thank you to all for your concern and well wishes.”

DC Studios co-chief James Gunn also informed fans of the change on Threads by writing: “Matt is still the director of ‘ The Batman 2 ‘ and always will be. I can’t express how profoundly grateful and moved we are by Steven’s offer to help him complete his vision.”

“I thought Matt Reeves’ work on ‘The Batman’ was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent,” Soderbergh added in his own statement. “The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.”

Along with Pattinson, other cast members for “The Batman Part II” include Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, Charles Dance, Brian Tyree Henry, Colin Farrell as the Penguin, Andy Serkis as Alfred Pennyworth and Jeffrey Wright as Commissioner Gordon.

article_text:
Disco Elysium

RPG sans nul autre pareil, Disco Elysium nous met aux commandes d’un détective décati, dont l’esprit embrumé est envahi par des voix intérieures. Ces dernières prennent la forme de compétences — logique, empathie, autorité ou imagination — qui interviennent dans les dialogues pour orienter nos décisions. Dans ce chef d’œuvre narratif, notre héros se construit ainsi dans une polyphonie aussi chaotique que savamment orchestrées.

2019 / ZA/UM / PC, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch

Dispatch

Dans un monde où les super-héros sont les gendarmes d’une ville en proie au chaos, nous voilà préposés au dispatch des urgences. Sur une carte de la ville, il faut envoyer chaque héros sur place, tout en maintenant le contact téléphonique avec eux. Gestion des équipes et des égos, tensions professionnelles et sentiments naissants : tout se mêle dans cette relecture aussi drôle que moderne du drama superhéroïque.

2025 / ADHOC STUDIO / PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch

Sovereign Tower

Chaque jour, les habitants de notre royaume se pressent à notre cour pour demander de l’aide ou se plaindre de leurs problèmes. À nous de trancher, mais aussi de choisir les chevalier·e·s capables d’exécuter chaque mission, selon leurs talents et leur caractère. Doté d’une écriture ciselée, ce petit RPG transforme l’exercice du pouvoir en une succession de dilemmes cornéliens, où chaque décision vient façonner notre règne.

2026 / WILD WITS GAMES / PC

Star Wars Zero Company

À la tête d’une troupe de mercenaires opérant dans l’ombre de la Guerre des Clones, il faut composer son escouade avant de l’envoyer au combat. Jedi, Mandalorien, ou encore droïde sur roulettes : chaque recrue possède ses compétences, son passif et ses affinités (ou l’inverse) avec ses collègues. Manière ô combien réjouissante de réaliser un fantasme de fan : monter le gang ultime de renégats dans cette galaxie très lointaine.

2026 / BIT REACTOR / PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S

Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave

Voilà 26 ans que la saga Fire Emblem mêle avec brio rigueur stratégique et soap opera médiéval. Ici, les liens que l’on tisse avec ses compagnons influencent directement leurs capacités sur le champ de bataille. Plus que jamais, la composition de l’équipe devient ainsi une affaire de cœur autant que de stratégie, chaque relation pouvant devenir une arme supplémentaire. D’une profondeur abyssale, ce nouvel opus élève son romanesque épique au rang d’art.

2026 / INTELLIGENT SYSTEMS, NINTENDO / Nintendo Switch 2

article_text:
Films and events

Family

Julián

Cartoon Saloon’s heartfelt animated tale about a boy who is proud to be different is a surefire hit.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Louise Bagnall

Screenwriter juliany taveras

With Knyght Darius Jack, Milcania Diaz-Rojas

Ireland-Luxembourg-Canada-Denmark 2026. 85min

Courtesy of Cartoon Saloon

Language English

Introduction

Young Julián, a bright child with a love of bling and sparkles, is sent to Brooklyn to stay with his Dominican grandmother. It’s tough initially, but when he learns about the forthcoming Mermaid Parade, something clicks – he is a mermaid! This flawless and uplifting film from LFF favourites Cartoon Saloon is a celebration of what it means to be young, different and loved.

Justin Johnson

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Iron Boy

With its smooth, hand-painted style, Iron Boy is a warm, moving animation about an 11-year-old boy who is forced to rethink his outlook on the world when he receives a life-changing diagnosis.

My Friend the Sun

In this engrossing and brightly coloured animated triumph, a young girl is transported to the home of the Mexican gods and has to fight to find her way back home.

The Mermaid Parade

This magical crafting adventure is inspired by the captivating film Julián.

title_original: Peter Nagy, 1959–2026: A Remembrance
editorial_title_zh: Peter Nagy, 1959–2026: A Remembrance
editorial_excerpt_zh: The American artist and co-founder of Nature Morte passed away in New Delhi, aged 66. Arthur Solway
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "News", "links": [{"text": "News", "url": "https://www.artasiapacific.com/tag/news/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Peter Nagy, 1959–2026: A Remembrance", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/size/w1200/2026/10/image--5-.png", "alt": "Peter Nagy, 1959–2026: A Remembrance", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "PETER NAGY . Courtesy Nature Morte, New Delhi/Mumbai.", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术家兼画廊主彼得·纳吉（Peter Nagy）于66岁去世后，社交媒体上涌现出大量悼念内容，令人心碎。这种哀思出现得如此迅捷，更平添了几分悲痛。坏消息似乎总是传得极快。他于10月13日在新德里的家中离世，他在那里生活了过去30年。死因是癌症。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我对彼得的记忆可以追溯到1983年在纽约的时候，当时我第一次见到他和加拿大艺术家艾伦·贝尔彻（Alan Belcher）。他们前一年刚刚共同创立了Nature Morte画廊：这家画廊当时位于东10街（East 10th Street）东村（East Village）一处狭窄且略显破旧的店面，靠近第二大道（Second Avenue）。东村当时的艺术界正确立其作为新艺术与新艺术家超级前卫基地的地位。杰夫·昆斯（Jeff Koons）、彼得·哈利（Peter Halley）以及彼得·纳吉当时由International With Monument画廊代理，那是另一个由艺术家迈耶·维斯曼（Meyer Vaisman）和利兹·库里（Liz Koury）创立的以观念艺术为宗旨的艺术家运营空间。该社区的其他画廊也如雨后春笋般涌现。充满激进气息与活力的闹市区，构成了对中产阶级化的苏荷区（SoHo）或保守的第57街（57th Street）以及沉闷的上城画廊的一个令人兴奋的替代选择，在一种逝去时代的后波希米亚式迷蒙中并存。不久，在阳光明媚的周末午后，停满双排车的大型豪华轿车里的收藏家和艺术顾问们便在东村画廊外闲等。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/image-31.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "PETER NAGY ,", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "STEVEN PARRINO ,", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "JOEL OTTERSON , and", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿伦·贝尔彻（ALAN BELCHER）、斯蒂芬·帕里诺（STEVEN PARRINO）、乔尔·奥特森（JOEL OTTERSON）与彼得·纳吉（PETER NAGY）在纽约204 E.10th Street的Nature Morte画廊装修期间，摄于1982年5月开业前一个月。罗宾·韦格林斯基（Robin Weglinski）摄影。图片由Nature Morte提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/image-32.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ALAN BELCHER . Photo by Mary Agnes Smith. Courtesy Nature Morte.", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "彼得1959年出生于康涅狄格州布里奇珀特，1981年毕业于纽约帕森斯设计学院（Parsons School of Design），获得传播设计学位。他对20世纪80年代初在市场上占主导地位的、流于表面且充满情绪驱动的绘画并不怎么感兴趣。Nature Morte画廊的艺术家们——其中包括同在帕森斯的同学乔尔·奥特森和斯蒂芬·帕里诺——更偏爱一种观念性方法，将包括露易丝·劳勒（Louise Lawler）、理查德·普林斯（Richard Prince）、谢莉·莱文（Sherrie Levine）和芭芭拉·克鲁格（Barbara Kruger）在内的“图片一代”（Pictures Generation）视作榜样。正如“图片一代”一样，Nature Morte的艺术家们对媒体、企业与消费文化、大众传播、包装以及广告表现出极大的兴趣——在审视关于本真性、原创性及其对整个社会之影响的假设的同时，面对信息的狂轰滥炸。彼得作为一名执业艺术家的个人创作——主要由黑白拼贴画、图表构成的层压静电复印件组成——正是扎根于这些诉求之中，始终沉浸在对信息传播永无止境的批判之中，这唯有他那渊博的艺术与艺术史知识方可匹敌。至于那个终极问题：什么是历史？", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Polaroids-by-Robin-Weglinski-of-Nature-Morte-over-the-years--New-York--NY--c-2-.-1980s-1-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他由纽约的Magenta Plains画廊代理，并于2020年成为一场名为“娱乐抹杀历史”（“Entertainment Erases History”）的大型回顾展的主角，展出了他于1982年至1992年期间创作的作品。该展览与Deitch Projects合作呈现，广受赞誉，并重新唤起了人们对彼得创作产出的兴趣。他的作品被纽约大都会艺术博物馆、惠特尼美国艺术博物馆、布鲁克林博物馆，以及休斯顿的梅尼尔收藏馆和纽约布法罗的布法罗AKG艺术博物馆（前身为奥尔布赖特-诺克斯美术馆）所收藏。他在国际上也享有盛誉，经常在伦敦、巴黎和科隆等欧洲城市举办机构展览。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾在Nature Morte举办过展览的画家朱莉娅·瓦赫特尔（Julia Wachtel）评论道：“他的一生确实奉献给了观看艺术，我的意思是跨越大陆和历史时期。他对艺术的热爱是无人能及的。他能记住一切。我从未见过哪个人的求知驱动力和记忆保持力能与彼得相媲美。我们去博物馆时，他几乎能一字不差地背诵出墙上的作品说明文字，并且他具有过目不忘的神奇能力，从不忘记吸收过的任何信息。他在这一点上相当了不起，独一无二。有时显得有些带刺、毫不留情，但对他所爱和关切的人却绝对忠诚。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/image-35-1.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/image-37-1.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "彼得·纳吉（PETER NAGY），《四大癌症标志》（Four Cancer Logos），1989年，木刻版画，111.7 x 111.7 cm，版数30之27（左）；以及《万（Quadrillion）》，1987年，布面丙烯，91.4 x 91.4 x 5 cm（右）。图片由艺术家及纽约Magenta Plains画廊提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "纽约的Nature Morte在运营7年之后于1988年关门歇业，部分原因在于艺术市场的低迷以及其他财务压力。彼得转而专注于他自己的艺术创作。他于1992年首次前往印度。他完全被迷住了；这是一个具有变革意义的时刻，让一切运转了起来。他于1997年永久搬迁至新德里，此后再未回头。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我想，在印度重塑Nature Morte一直是梦想的一部分，而彼得在纽约风格画廊模式方面的专业知识、经验和见识，对于年轻一代的南亚艺术家而言无疑令人兴奋。彼得内心是一位文化建筑师，是在全球范围内精明且深谙此道的桥梁建造者。早期，他大力推崇苏博德·古普塔（Subodh Gupta）、吉蒂什·卡拉特（Jitish Kallat）以及摄影师达亚尼塔·辛格（Dayanita Singh）等众多艺术家的作品，他们后来都取得了极大的职业成功，并赢得了更广泛的国际受众。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_9259-1.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_0928.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "（从左至右）阿拉尼·博斯（ARANI BOSE）与彼得·纳吉（PETER NAGY）在艺术家工作室的合影。玛丽娜·托马斯（Marina Thomas）摄影并提供；以及阿拉尼·博斯与彼得·纳吉在威尼斯肖像。Bose Pacia摄影并提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿拉尼·博斯（Arani Bose）是一位起到关键作用的早期商业合作伙伴，正是他为后来的道路奠定了基础。他的画廊 Bose Pacia 曾在纽约苏荷区开店。博斯与新德里的 Nature Morte 进行了合作并提供了资金支持。“彼得将印度当代艺术的粗犷边缘与跳动脉搏，”博斯回忆道，“注入了20世纪末苏荷区严肃、成熟且死板的艺术基础设施中。连续好几年，彼得每年夏天都会在手提箱里塞满来自印度有前途的艺术家的作品，并与他那总是非常时尚的服装混搭在一起。随后，他在我们位于百老汇、靠近王子街的画廊里挂起了一场场精彩且看似刻不容缓的展览，向纽约人打开了心扉，让他们了解整个次大陆各地正在发生的鲜为人知、具有颠覆性的艺术行动。我们在南德里的 A1 Neeti Bagh 开设了 Nature Morte 的第一个永久据点。通过这一干预，我们开始引入一些枯燥的专业精神、规程以及标准化基础设施，这对于在印度培育一个稳定、可靠的艺术市场而言是必不可少的。彼得具有得天独厚的优势，能够将地球两端的艺术世界进行异花授粉。为什么人们会倾听并重视他的话？因为他的才智、他的诚实、他的机智，以及他那尖锐、深刻的散文笔触。凭借他的个性和他的笔，他帮助定义了来自该次大陆的一代艺术家。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "苏博德·古普塔（Subodh Gupta）的加盟是该画廊早期成功的关键。彼得于1997年在纽约首次见到这位艺术家。“当彼得和我再次在印度相遇时，他记得我们第一次见面时的所有事情，”古普塔回忆道，“我们成为了密友，并一起合作了29年。彼得热爱艺术。他总是在谈论艺术和艺术家，这就是他的生活。那种激情非常特别。他在自己周围建立了一个伟大的家庭，我们分享了如此多的欢笑和快乐。我从他的故事和我们的交谈中学到了很多。那些在一起的时刻将永远留在我的记忆中。在印度几乎没有空间容纳实验艺术的时候，他支持那些创作截然不同作品的年轻艺术家。他无畏而诚实。没有人像他那样给予我如此大的自由，让我以自己的方式展示我的作品。彼得用我的个展来开启他的新画廊空间，这是一份我会永远珍惜的信任之举。他的离去对印度的艺术界而言是一个巨大的损失，对我来说，这也失去了我曾与之分享大半生的一位挚友。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_1743.JPEG", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_4086-1.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "（左起）阿拉尼·博斯、苏博德·古普塔和彼得·纳吉（左）；彼得·纳吉与巴蒂·科尔（Bharti Kher）肖像（右）。致谢：苏博德·古普塔。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然有些人肯定对他的双重抱负——即一方面是一位严肃的执业艺术家，另一方面又是画廊主和策展人——抱有怀疑态度，但彼得从未退缩。创意与商业从来都不是问题。他将整个事业视为完全共生的关系。然而毫无疑问，艺术和艺术家永远是第一位的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术家吉蒂什·卡拉特（Jitish Kallat）回忆起1997年在孟买的个人首展上遇到彼得的情景。“他为我1999年纽约首展的图录写了一篇评论文章，我深情地回想起他对艺术写作的天赋。他的文字具有一种奇妙的清澈感，几乎带有意识流的特质，以及一种激进的诚实语调。在共同布展时，我们偶尔会有分歧，彼得往往希望在展览中纳入比我设想中更多的作品。然而我常常会回过头来，理解他的意图以及他是如何将事物组合在一起的。我记得当他在斋浦尔策划第一座雕塑公园时，他几乎处于一种狂喜的状态。我认为彼得骨子里的艺术家特质始终存在于他策划展览的方式之中。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/DSC00675.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉蒂什·卡拉特与", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "彼得·纳吉在新德里比卡内尔大厦（Bikaner House）当代艺术中心举行的艺术家个展“对一张纸质天空的猜想”（“Conjectures on a Paper Sky”）预展上，2026年。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2018年，我将英国艺术家理查德·朗（Richard Long）介绍给彼得，参与他的雕塑公园项目。朗深情地回忆起彼得以及他委托自己为马达文德拉宫（Madhavendra Palace）创作的不朽作品《石头之河》（River of Stones）。“由于庭院入口相当狭窄，我们最终用自行车三轮车把我的石头运了进去。彼得非常精明，个性张扬。他自己也是一名艺术家，所以我们相处得很好。他是一个非常真实且富有磁场的人。我会永远记住他。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在20世纪80年代末，彼得和我有很多合作的机会，当时我将他介绍给我的父亲卡尔·索尔韦（Carl Solway），我父亲拥有一家画廊，对资助和出版年轻艺术家的作品版画很感兴趣。当时我在其中发挥了很大的作用。早期在纽约经营 Nature Morte 时频繁参展的艺术家乔尔·奥特森（Joel Peter Nagy, 1959–2026: A Remembrance

PETER NAGY . Courtesy Nature Morte, New Delhi/Mumbai.

The outpouring on social media following the death of artist and gallerist Peter Nagy, at age 66, was heartbreaking. It felt even more distressing by how instantaneously it appeared. Bad news, it seems, travels fast. He died at home on October 13 in New Delhi, where he had lived for the past 30 years. The cause was cancer.

My memories of Peter go back to 1983 in New York, when I first met him and Canadian artist Alan Belcher. They had just co-founded Nature Morte the year before: the gallery occupied a narrow and slightly shabby East Village storefront on East 10th Street, off of Second Avenue. The East Village scene was establishing itself as the ultra-trendy outpost for new art and artists. Jeff Koons, Peter Halley, and Peter Nagy were then represented by the gallery International With Monument, another artist-run space with a mandate for the conceptual, founded by artists Meyer Vaisman and Liz Koury. Other neighborhood galleries, too, were cropping up. Radical and vibrant, the downtown scene was an exciting alternative to gentrified SoHo or old guard 57th Street and the stuffy uptown galleries, co-existing in a kind of post-bohemian haze of a bygone era. Soon, the collectors and art advisors in double-parked limos idled outside the East Village galleries on sunny weekend afternoons.

PETER NAGY ,

STEVEN PARRINO ,

JOEL OTTERSON , and

ALAN BELCHER during the renovation of Nature Morte on 204 E.10th Street, New York, a month before the opening in May 1982. Photo by Robin Weglinski. Courtesy Nature Morte.

ALAN BELCHER . Photo by Mary Agnes Smith. Courtesy Nature Morte.

Born in 1959 in Bridgeport, Connecticut, Peter graduated from New York’s Parsons School of Design in 1981 with a degree in communication design. He wasn’t particularly interested in the sloppy, emotionally driven painting that was market dominant during the early 1980s. The artists at Nature Morte, among them fellow Parsons classmates Joel Otterson and Steven Parrino, favored a more conceptual approach, looking to the Pictures Generation that included artists Louise Lawler, Richard Prince, Sherrie Levine, and Barbara Kruger as role models. Like the Pictures Generation, the artists of Nature Morte were keenly interested in media, corporate and consumer culture, mass communication, packaging, and advertising—the barrage of information while scrutinizing assumptions about authenticity, originality, and its impact on society at large. Peter’s own work as a practicing artist—primarily consisting of black-and-white collages, laminated Xeroxes of diagrammatic compositions—was rooted in these imperatives, always engaged by an insatiable critique on the transmission of information, matched only by his profound knowledge of art and art history. And to the question itself: What is history?

He was represented by Magenta Plains in New York and, in 2020, was the subject of a comprehensive survey titled “Entertainment Erases History,” featuring works made between 1982 and 1992. The exhibition, presented in collaboration with Deitch Projects, received great acclaim and renewed interest in Peter’s output. His works were collected by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Brooklyn Museum, as well as the Menil Collection in Houston and the Buffalo AKG Art Museum (formerly the Albright-Knox Art Gallery) in Buffalo, New York. He had an international presence as well, frequently holding institutional shows in London, Paris, and Cologne, among other European cities.

Painter Julia Wachtel, who exhibited at Nature Morte, commented: “His life really was devoted to looking at art, and I mean across continents and time periods. His love of art was unmatched by anyone. He remembered everything. I have never met anyone with the same voracious drive and memory retention as Peter. We’d go to museums and he could practically regurgitate the wall labels verbatim, and he had the uncanny ability of total recall, never forgetting any information he had absorbed. He was quite amazing that way, one of a kind. Prickly at times, and taking no prisoners, but completely loyal to those he loved and cared about.”

PETER NAGY , Four Cancer Logos , 1989 , woodcut, 111.7 x 111.7 cm, edition 27 of 30 (left); and Quadrillion , 1987, acrylic on canvas, 91.4 x 91.4 x 5 cm (right). Courtesy the artist and Magenta Plains, New York.

Nature Morte in New York closed up shop in 1988 after a seven-year run, partly due to a lull in the art market and other financial pressures. Peter focused on his own art. His first trip to India was in 1992. He was absolutely spellbound; it was a transformative moment, setting things in motion. He relocated permanently to New Delhi in 1997 and never looked back.

Reinventing Nature Morte in India was always a part of the dream, I suppose, and Peter’s expertise, experience, and knowledge of a New York-style gallery model was surely exciting for a younger generation of South Asian artists. Peter was a cultural architect at heart, an astute and savvy bridge builder on a global scale. Early on he championed the works of Subodh Gupta, Jitish Kallat, and photographer Dayanita Singh, among many others, all of whom went on to sustain highly successful careers, reaching a wider international audience.

(Left to right) Portrait of ARANI BOSE and PETER NAGY at an artist’s studio. Photo by and courtesy Marina Thomas; and portrait of ARANI BOSE and PETER NAGY in Venice. Photo by and courtesy Bose Pacia.

An instrumental early business partner who helped pave the way was Arani Bose, whose gallery Bose Pacia had set up shop in SoHo in New York. Bose partnered and financed Nature Morte in New Delhi. “Peter injected the raw edge and beating pulse of contemporary art happening in India,” Bose reflected, “into the serious, established, and staid art infrastructure of SoHo toward the end of the 20th century. Each summer for several years, Peter would pack his suitcases with art from promising artists in India, intermingled with his always very fashionable clothing. He would then hang beautiful and seemingly urgent shows in our gallery at Broadway, near Prince Street, opening New Yorkers’ minds to the little known, subversive acts of art happening all over the subcontinent. We opened the first permanent home of Nature Morte at A1 Neeti Bagh in South Delhi. With this intervention, we began to introduce a bit of the boring professionalism or protocol and standardized infrastructure necessary to grow a stable, reliable art market in India. Peter was uniquely positioned to cross-pollinate the art worlds at two ends of the globe. Why did people listen and heed his words? Because of his intellect, his honesty, his wit, and his biting, incisive prose. With his personality and his pen, he helped to define a generation of artists from the subcontinent.”

Pivotal to the early success of the gallery was the representation of Subodh Gupta. Peter first met the artist in New York in 1997. “When Peter and I met again in India, he remembered everything from that first meeting,” Gupta recalled. “We became close friends and worked together for 29 years. Peter loved art. He was always talking about art and artists, it was his life. That passion was something very special. He created a great family around him, and we shared so much laughter and fun. I learned so much from his stories and our conversations. Those moments together will always stay with me. At a time when there was little space in India for experimental art, he supported young artists making very different kinds of work. He was fearless and honest. No one gave me as much freedom to show my work in my own way. Peter opened his new gallery spaces with my solo shows, a gesture of trust I will always treasure. His loss is immense for art in India and, for me, it is also the loss of a dear friend with whom I shared so much of my life.”

Portrait of (left to right) ARANI BOSE , SUBODH GUPTA , and PETER NAGY (left); and portrait of PETER NAGY with BHARTI KHER (right). Courtesy Subodh Gupta.

While some were certainly skeptical of his tandem ambitions—that of a serious practicing artist versus gallerist and curator—Peter never flinched. Creativity and commerce were never an issue. He saw the whole enterprise as completely symbiotic. However, the art and artists, without question, always came first.

Artist Jitish Kallat remembers meeting Peter at his solo debut in Mumbai in 1997. “He wrote an essay for the catalog of my first New York solo show in 1999, and I fondly recall his flair for writing about art. His writing had a wonderful lucidity, an almost stream-of-consciousness quality, and a radical honesty of tone. While installing shows together we would occasionally disagree, with Peter often wanting to include more works in an exhibition than I had imagined. Yet I would often come around to see what he had in mind and how he brought things together. I remember him being almost euphoric when he curated the first Sculpture Park in Jaipur. I think the artist in Peter was always present in the way he approached curating.”

JITISH KALLAT and

PETER NAGY at the preview of the artist’s solo exhibition “Conjectures on a Paper Sky” at the Centre for Contemporary Art, Bikaner House, New Delhi, 2026.

I introduced British artist Richard Long to Peter for his Sculpture Park project in 2018. Long fondly remembers Peter and the monumental work River of Stones he had commissioned him to create for the Madhavendra Palace. “Because the courtyard entrance was quite narrow we ended up having my stones brought in on bicycle rickshaws. Peter was very smart and had a big personality. He was an artist himself, so we got along very well. He was a very authentic and charismatic man. I will always remember him.”

Peter and I had a number of opportunities to work together in the late 1980s when I introduced him to my father, Carl Solway, who had a gallery and was interested in financing and publishing editions with young artists. I had a big hand in this at the time. The artist Joel Otterson, who frequently exhibited in those early New York days of Nature Morte, remarked, “Peter was a unique human. He was a conduit that connected people with life-changing effects. ‘Curiosity will keep us young,’ Peter would say. He said this when we were only in our early 20s.”

He is survived by his brother Paul Nagy as well as his longtime partner, Timmy Martin. In keeping with his wishes the galleries in New Delhi and its Mumbai outpost will continue under the supervision of senior director and business partner for the last 13 years, Aparajita Jain. A traditional Hindu cremation took place on October 14. India was Peter’s spiritual home (though I can almost hear him cackling—and he could cackle—by my saying so). He loved India and was deeply committed to the life he had created for himself there. Friendships that endure for 40 years or more are nothing if not truly significant. Like so many others, I will miss him.

Arthur Solway is the author of two collections of poetry, Friday Night, Shanghai (2023) and Siddhartha On Fire (2023), the latter of which received the 2024 San Francisco Book Festival Prize in Poetry. He presently lives in Santa Cruz, California.

on canvas, 91.4 x 91.4 x 5 cm (右) . 艺术家和Magenta Plains, 纽约。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nature Morte 在纽约关闭了商店在1988年7年后,部分是由于艺术市场和其他财务压力,彼得专注于自己的艺术,他的第一次去印度是在1992年,他绝对是紧张的,这是一个转变的时刻,把事情在动作中,他在1997年永久搬到新德里,从来没有回头看。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我想,在印度重新发明自然死亡一直是梦想的一部分,彼得的专业知识,经验和知识,一个纽约风格的画廊模型肯定是令人兴奋的年轻一代的南亚艺术家。彼得是一个文化建筑师在心脏,一个聪明和有智慧的桥梁建设者在全球范围内。职业生涯,达到更广泛的国际观众。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_9259-1.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_0928.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "(左向右) 艺术家工作室中的ARANI BOSE和PETER NAGY的肖像; 由和慈善玛丽娜·托马斯的照片; 和在威尼斯的ARANI BOSE和PETER NAGY的肖像; 由和慈善博塞·帕西亚的照片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一个有工具的早期业务合作伙伴,帮助走路是阿拉尼·博塞,其画廊博塞·帕西亚在纽约的索霍设立了商店,博塞合作并资助了新德里的自然死亡,“彼得注入了在印度发生的当代艺术的原始边缘和打击脉冲,”博塞反映,“在索霍的严重,建立,并保持到20世纪末的艺术基础设施。印度,与他总是非常时尚的服装混乱,他会随后挂着美丽而似乎紧急的表演在我们的画廊在布罗德威,靠近普林斯街,打开纽约人的头脑到不熟悉的,破坏性的艺术行为发生在整个地下大陆。 我们打开了第一个永久的自然死亡在A1 Neeti Bagh在南德里。 通过这种干预,我们开始介绍一些无聊的专业主义或协议和标准化的基础设施,需要在印度发展一个稳定的,可靠的艺术市场。独一无二的位置,在世界两端交叉的艺术世界,为什么人们倾听和赞扬他的话语?因为他的智力,他的诚实,他的证人,和他的痛苦,刺激的预言,他的个性和他的笔,他帮助定义一代艺术家从大陆。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "画廊早期成功的关键是代表Subodh Gupta. 彼得第一次见到艺术家在纽约1997年,“当彼得和我在印度再次见面时,他记得这一切,从第一次见面,”Gupta回忆道,“我们成为亲密的朋友,并一起工作了29年。这些时刻将永远留在我身边,在印度实验艺术的空间很少的时候,他支持年轻艺术家做各种各样的作品,他是无畏的,诚实的,没有人给了我那么多的自由,以我自己的方式展示我的作品,彼得用我的单曲展开了他的新画廊空间,一个信任的动作我将永远宝藏,他的损失是印度艺术的巨大,对我来说,也是一个亲爱的朋友的损失,我和他分享了很多生活。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_1743.JPEG", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/IMG_4086-1.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "(左向右) ARANI BOSE , SUBODH GUPTA , 和 PETER NAGY (左); 和 PETER NAGY 与 BHARTI KHER (右) 的肖像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然有些人对他的同步野心特别怀疑 - 对一个严肃的练习艺术家对画家和校长的野心 - 彼得从来没有跳过,创造力和商业从来没有成为一个问题,他看到了整个企业是完全同情的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术家吉蒂什·卡拉特在1997年在孟买独奏演唱会上与彼得相遇,“他在1999年写了一篇论文,我深深地记得他对艺术写作的热情,他的写作具有美妙的清晰度,几乎是意识的质量,以及激进的声音诚实。我记得他在吉普赛的第一座雕塑公园治愈时几乎是无情的,我认为彼得的艺术家在他接近治愈的方式总是存在的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/DSC00675.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉特斯·卡拉特和", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "彼得·纳吉在艺术家在现代艺术中心,比卡纳家,新德里,2026年展出的单曲展览“纸天上的概念”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我介绍了英国艺术家理查德·隆格到彼得他的雕塑公园项目2018年,长久深地记得彼得和他委托他为马达文德拉宫创建的纪念作品河石,“因为花园的入口相当狭窄,我们结束了我的石头带到自行车里克萨夫,彼得非常聪明,有一个伟大的个性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "彼得和我有机会在晚些时候一起工作。 1980 我把他介绍给我父亲卡尔·索尔威,他有一个画廊,他有兴趣与年轻艺术家资助和出版出版的出版物,我当时在这一点上有很大的手。艺术家乔尔·奥特森,他经常在纽约早期的自然死亡日展出,“彼得是一个独特的人,他是一个行为,将人们与生活变化的影响联系在一起。我们说过这一点,当我们只有在20年代初才。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他被他的兄弟保罗·内格和他的长期合作伙伴蒂米·马丁生存了,根据他的愿望,新德里的画廊和孟买的展览会将继续在上13年的首席执行官和商业合作伙伴阿帕拉吉塔·贾因的监督下,印度在10月14日举行了一场传统的印度化,印度是彼得的精神家园(也许我几乎听到他摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇摇。40年或更长的友谊,如果不是真正重要的,就没有什么,就像许多其他人一样,我会错过他。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿瑟·索尔威(Arthur Solway)是诗歌的两个收藏品的作者,星期五夜,上海(2023)和火上的西德哈塔(2023),其中后者获得了2024年圣弗朗西斯书节诗歌奖。", "translated": true}]

HERMÈSTORIES: AN ADVENTURE TAKES THE STAGE / Oct 24 – Nov 8, 2026 /

Play & Exhibition / 4.30pm and 7.30pm (Weekdays) 2.30pm and 5.30pm (Weekends) No play on 26 October and 2 November Register

Exhibition Only Sessions every 30 minutes 11am to 7pm (Weekdays) 10.30am to 5pm (Weekends) Register

Freespace West Kowloon Cultural District Hong Kong

hermes.com

EXPERIENCE A PLAYFUL AND POETIC THEATRICAL CREATION IN HONG KONG INSPIRED BY THE STORIES OF HERMÈS

Hermès invites the public to discover its story and its iconic objects in a show with surrealist touches, written by Pauline Bayle and directed by Joe Hufton. Accompanying the play, an original exhibition offers insights into the house’s spirit through a journey that combines bold staging with a new twist on oral tradition.

On set, stage props transform into ingenious tools to illustrate some of the house’s major events and surprising moments that symbolize the continuous momentum of Hermès. The diversity of the house’s sixteen métiers is showcased.

The exhibition invites the audience to wander through an installation designed like a theatre storeroom. It offers an opportunity to see these iconic objects at close quarters, to discover their history and their artisanal and creative dimensions.

The bond between past and present is felt deeply in this theatrical saga that looks firmly to the future.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Photo Review 是一本创办于1976年的摄影评论杂志，将于2026年10月24日星期六下午4点在宾夕法尼亚州费城赛斯街1916号（邮编：19103）的摩尔艺术设计学院（Moore College of Art & Design）举办盛大的年度慈善拍卖会，以庆祝其50周年。此次拍卖会将呈献从19世纪到当代的众多重要摄影作品。买家可以在线预览现场拍卖：https://photoreview.org/events/2026-benefit-auction/。", "links": [{"text": "https://photoreview.org/events/2026-benefit-auction/", "url": "https://photoreview.org/events/2026-benefit-auction/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "缺席竞标可通过发送电子邮件至 [email protected] 或致电 215/891-0214 在2026年10月23日美东时间下午6点前提交。The Photo Review 将提供其“结束本次拍卖”（END THIS AUCTION）功能。对任何未售出的拍品出价最高估价，您的出价即被视为中标，且该作品将从拍卖中撤回。", "links": [{"text": "[email protected]", "url": "https://loeildelaphotographie.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "您还可以在 LiveAuctioneers 上注册并竞标：https://www.liveauctioneers.com/catalog/435082_the-2026-photo-review-benefit-auction/。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "预展将于10月23日星期五中午12点至下午5点，以及10月24日星期日中午12点至下午3点在摩尔艺术学院举行，周六下午3点至4点还将举办招待会。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
The Photo Review , a critical journal of photography founded in 1976, will celebrate its 50th anniversary with a spectacular Annual Benefit Auction on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 4 p.m. at the Moore College of Art & Design, 1916 Race Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103. The auction will offer a significant array of photographs from the 19th century to the present. Buyers can preview the live auction online at https://photoreview.org/events/2026-benefit-auction/ .

Absentee bids can be received by 6 p.m. EST on October 23, 2026, by emailing [email protected] or calling 215/891-0214. The Photo Review will offer its END THIS AUCTION feature. Bid the high estimate on any unsold lot and your bid will be considered the winning bid and the work will be withdrawn from the auction.

You can also register and bid on LiveAuctioneers: https://www.liveauctioneers.com/catalog/435082_the-2026-photo-review-benefit-auction/.

A preview will be held at Moore on Friday, October 23, 12–5 PM, and Saturday, October 24, 12 – 3 PM with a reception from 3–4 PM on Saturday.

rot，即思维退化）之间左右摇摆。这种状况显然让拉贡拉杰怒不可遏，与此同时，他自己也是这片喧嚣的一部分。因为他的发言自然是在 TikTok 上进行实时直播，并被输入到我们当今时代的无垠数据池中。这段视频究竟会被人类观看，还是仅仅充当机器的训练内容，目前尚不得而知。", "links": [{"text": "der US-Streamer Lagonraj in die Kamera", "url": "https://www.instagram.com/lagonraj/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉贡拉杰如今也获得了一定程度的艺术声誉，因为他被描述的那段剪辑正是美国电影人亚瑟·贾法的新作《N****s in Omelas》的一部分。这位导演对“同时性”并不陌生，因为这是他视觉艺术创作的概念核心。他将来自各行各业的现成照片和电影片段剪辑成宏大的拼贴画，其中没有任何等级之分，私人家庭录像与好莱坞场景、迈克尔·杰克逊（Michael Jackson）的演唱会以及马丁·路德·金（Martin Luther King）标志性的“我有一个梦想”演讲占据着相同的空间。这里没有上下文，每个人都必须自行决定是什么在挑动自己的神经。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "现年66岁的亚瑟·贾法可以说是数字时代黑人贫穷艺术（Arte Povera）的奠基人，在这个时代，无论画面像素多么模糊，任何类型的内容都可以成为挪用创作的素材。德国艺术家希托·史德尔（Hito Steyerl）曾将“贫瘠的图像”（poor image）称为“表象阶级社会中的流氓无产阶级”以及“视听制作的废墟”。亚瑟·贾法将这些瓦砾带回大银幕，并用它们构建出带有激动人心配乐的崇高艺术作品，恐怖与魅力在其中以幽灵般的方式交织，美国的大众视觉世界则始终诉说着奴役的暴力遗产，同时也诉说着抵抗与黑人卓越（black excellence）。", "links": [{"text": "die \"Trümmer der true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《N****s in Omelas》的欧洲首映式同时也是一个终点。它于周四晚在柏林茱莉亚·施托谢克基金会（JSF）举行，也是位于莱比锡大街（Leipziger Straße）东柏林板式住宅群之间的这个地点的最后一项活动。运营十年后，这位来自杜塞尔多夫的收藏家将关闭其柏林分支机构，并将精力集中于莱茵河畔的主馆以及国际项目。", "links": [{"text": "schließt die Düsseldorfer Sammlerin ihre Berliner Dependance", "url": "以亚瑟·贾法的电影作为柏林之行的收官之作，形成了一个完美的闭环。因为在2018年，施托谢克曾在这里举办过他的首次德国个展“A series of utterly improbable yet extraordinary renditions”，而正是在那个时候，这位导演的角色开始发生转变：从艺术界备受崇敬但行事低调的“艺术家心中的艺术家”（artist's "https://www.monopol-magazin.de/arthur-jafa-goldener-loewe"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "施托谢克基金会的闭幕之夜再次完美诠释了这个地方的特质。十年来，这里展出了值得一看的“基于时间的媒体艺术”（time-based media art），这也是施托谢克对其收藏重心的称呼。换句话说，任何对录像艺术的过去和现在感兴趣的人，都几乎无法绕过柏林 JSF，因为它比大多数博物馆都更专业（且资金更充足）地致力于这一媒介。但这从来都不是全部的故事。因为要欣赏这些艺术，少不了伴随而来的社会奇观。在开幕式之前，排队的队伍达到了类似伯恩黑姆（Berghain）的规模，沿着原本并不怎么光鲜的莱比锡大街拐角绵延不绝；这里的观众比柏林其他机构更加前卫、更加国际化也更加老练。一切都是时尚/设计/艺术/创意产业/夜生活的混合体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术马戏团竞技场中的所有矛盾", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种混合或许解释了为什么这个地方会引发如此大的争议。正如许多充满伤感的 Instagram 告别帖所显示的那样，施托谢克基金会一直是策展人和艺术家们的重要聚集地。按照这种解读，柏林固定场馆的关闭是这座首都作为艺术滋养地衰落的又一迹象。另一方面，文化界的某些小众群体则尽量不想与这位女亿万富翁的私人机构沾边，并将其视为资本驱动、对注意力极度饥渴的艺术泡沫的一个症状。", "links": [{"text": "den Niedergang der Hauptstadt als Kunstnährboden", "url": "https://www.monopol-magazin.de/post-cool-berlin"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在新冠疫情期间，还曾爆发过关于施托谢克家族企业的辩论，该企业在纳粹时期曾从中获得经济利益。就连讽刺作家扬·伯默曼（Jan Böhmermann）也在 ZDF 电视台对此进行了显赫的报道，艺术家莱昂·卡哈内（Leon Kahane）也围绕这一主题举办了展览。因此，许多线索在施托谢克收藏中交织在一起。批评性艺术的线索，以及关于德国经济中纳粹遗产以及“具纳粹背景的人”的问题——正如艺术家莫什塔里·希拉尔（Moshtari Hilal）和辛图詹·瓦拉达拉贾（Sinthujan Varatharajah）在2021年一场引发热烈讨论的 Instagram 对话系列中所表述的那样。", "links": [{"text": "eine Debatte um das Familienunternehmen der Stoscheks", "url": "https://www.monopol-magazin.de/moshtari-hilal-menschen-mit-nazi-hintergrund-kritik-ist-das-gegenteil-von-gleichgueltigkeit"}, {"text": "während der NS-Zeit wirtschaftlich profitierte", "url": "https://www.faz.net/aktuell/feuilleton/kunstmarkt/hito-steyerl-julia-stoschek-und-die-firma-brose-18538900.html"}, {"text": "eine Ausstellung zu dem Thema", "url": "https://www.monopol-magazin.de/moshtari-hilal-menschen-mit-nazi-hintergrund-kritik-ist-das-gegenteil-von-gleichgueltigkeit"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这显然没有阻挡观众的热情。就在最后一个夜晚，衣着光鲜的人们依然挤满了JSF柏林馆的走廊和放映厅，观看贾法的电影。如果说有一部作品能够契合艺术圈所制造的种种矛盾，那大概就是他的这部作品。它展现了美国历史与现实每个毛孔中渗透的残酷种族主义，但同时又将其转化为一种催眠般的视觉洪流供人消费。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "关键在于忍耐", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，《N****s in Omelas》的运作方式与以往的电影略有不同。这一次，剪辑不再以快速而有节奏的步伐呼啸而过——社交媒体无休止的短视频流现实，或许在这一点上早已超越了艺术。相反，人们现在必须历经数分钟去熬过某些折磨人的片段。对黑人男性的血腥屠杀大片，对精神错乱的迈克尔·杰克逊面临虐童指控的采访。关键在于忍耐——对片中主角和观众而言皆是如此。人们必须不断进行自我校准。此处需要的是同理心、讽刺还是分析？视觉上的解脱（黑人花样滑冰运动员苏亚·博纳利优雅的后空翻、一个在摆造型视频中不小心朝天花板开枪并被女友狠狠训斥的白人老兄）稍纵即逝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "随后，整部作品毫无歧义且毫无准备地以现实当代残垣断壁中的末日景象收尾：一架无人机飞越加沙一片完全被毁的住宅区，人们像在反乌托邦电子游戏中一样四处游荡。在吉恩·怀尔德于背景中呢喃着《查理和巧克力工厂》中甜腻的音乐剧热门曲目《纯净的想象》（Pure Imagination）的同时，手机视频中展示出了浑身是血的儿童，这彻底击碎了亚瑟·贾法之前建立的所有戏仿、烟雾弹和虚构层级。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是该片一个残酷、不可调和的结局，它直接通往绝大多数当代艺术争论的归零地：即对中东战争的立场表态，以及关于在德国对此必须/被允许/能够说些什么的讨论。在这里，语境以及如何对这些图像进行归类的问题实际上就是一切，因此片尾的蒙太奇为不同的解读留出了巨大空间。但这些影像终究也是我们世界的一部分，正实时流传，并在艺术空间与观众的智能手机上要求得到回应。某一刻，朱莉娅·斯托舍克基金会的银幕变黑了。但人们知道，这绝不是图像洪流的终点。", article_text:
Als letzten Akt vor der Schließung hat die Julia Stoschek Foundation in Berlin den neuen Film von US-Künstler Arthur Jafa gezeigt. Der Abend brachte auf den Punkt, warum dieser Ort so polarisiert hat – und endete in der Apokalypse

"The world is drowning in noise", sagt der US-Streamer Lagonraj in die Kamera . Sein Gesicht füllt das Hochformat des Bildes fast ganz aus, das lange schwarze Haar fällt ihm denkerhaft in die Stirn. Er scheint in einem Auto zu sitzen, die Botschaft muss aber offenbar unbedingt raus. Die Welt versinkt im Lärm, im ständigen medialen Geräusch, das die Menschen so vollumfänglich umgibt und absorbiert, dass sie keinen klaren Gedanken mehr fassen können und zwischen Dauerempörung und brain rot , also Gehirnzersetzung, hin und hertaumeln. Lagonraj bringt dieser Umstand sichtlich in Rage, gleichzeitig ist er ein Teil dieses Rauschens. Denn seine Ansprache wird natürlich in Echtzeit bei TikTok übertragen und in den unermesslichen Datenpool unserer Gegenwart eingespeist. Ob das Video von Menschen gesehen wird oder lediglich als Trainingscontent für Maschinen dient, ist erstmal ungewiss.

Zu etwas künstlerischem Ruhm hat es Lagonraj nun aber gebracht, denn der beschriebene Clip ist ein Teil des neuen Werks " N****s in Omelas" des US-Filmemachers Arthur Jafa. Der Regisseur kennt sich mit Gleichzeitigkeit aus, denn sie ist das konzeptuelle Zentrum seiner Arbeit in der bildenden Kunst. Er montiert gefundene Fotos und Filmclips verschiedenster Herkunft zu monumentalen Collagen, in denen es keine Hierarchien gibt und private Homevideos den gleichen Raum einnehmen wie Hollywood-Szenen, ein Michael-Jackson-Konzert und Martin Luther Kings ikonische "I have a dream"-Rede. Es gibt keinen Kontext, jeder muss selbst entscheiden, wovon er oder sie sich provozieren lässt.

Arthur Jafa (66) ist so etwas wie der Begründer einer Schwarzen Arte Povera im digitalen Zeitalter, in dem jede Art von Footage zum Material für kreative Aneignung werden kann, in welch pixeliger Qualität es auch immer vorliegen mag. Die deutsche Künstlerin Hito Steyerl hat das "poor image", das arme Bild, mal als "Lumpenproletariat in der Klassengesellschaft der Erscheinungen" und die "Trümmer der audiovisuellen Produktion" bezeichnet . Arthur Jafa bringt diesen Schutt zurück auf die große Leinwand und baut daraus erhabene Kunstwerke mit mitreißendem Soundtrack, in denen sich Grauen und Glamour auf gespenstische Weise verstricken und die populären Bildwelten der USA immer vom gewaltvollen Erbe der Sklaverei, aber auch von Widerstand und black excellence erzählen.

Eine Premiere als Ende

Die Europa-Premiere von " N****s in Omelas" war gleichzeitig ein Ende. Sie fand am Donnerstagabend in der Julia Stoschek Foundation (JSF) in Berlin statt und war der letzte Programmpunkt am Standort zwischen den Ost-Berliner Plattenbauten in der Leipziger Straße. Nach zehn Jahren schließt die Düsseldorfer Sammlerin ihre Berliner Dependance und will sich auf das Haupthaus im Rheinland und internationale Projekte konzentrieren.

Mit dem Arthur-Jafa-Film als Berliner Finale schließt sich ein Kreis. Denn 2018 zeigte Stoschek hier dessen erste deutsche Einzelausstellung "A series of utterly improbable yet extraordinary renditions", genau dann, als sich die Rolle des Regisseurs zu wandeln begann: vom im Betrieb verehrten, aber diskreten artist's artist zum globalen Kunstsuperstar mit goldenem Venedig-Löwen , Art-Basel-Präsenz und Fashion-Week-Einladungen. Disclaimer: Die Autorin dieses Textes hat damals als Studentin in der Ausstellung Führungen gegeben - und wird einige der Bildschnipsel aus der flackernden Videoinstallation "Apex" wohl nie wieder aus dem Kopf bekommen.

Der Abschlussabend in der Stoschek Foundation brachte noch einmal auf den Punkt, was diesen Ort ausgemacht hat. Es gab hier zehn Jahre lang sehenswerte Ausstellungen mit "zeitbasierter Medienkunst", wie Stoschek den Schwerpunkt ihrer Sammlung gern nennt. Anders ausgedrückt: Wer sich für die Vergangenheit und Gegenwart von Videokunst interessiert, kam an der JSF Berlin kaum vorbei, weil sie sich dem Medium professioneller (und besser finanziert) widmet als die meisten Museen. Aber das war nie die ganze Geschichte. Denn die Kunst war nicht ohne soziales Spektakel zu haben. Vor den Eröffnungen bogen sich Schlangen von Berghain-Ausmaß um die Ecken der sonst eher wenig glamourösen Leipziger Straße; das Publikum war hipper, internationaler und abgebrühter als an anderen Berliner Institutionen. Alles Mode slash Design slash Kunst slash Kreativindustrie slash Nachtleben.

Alle Widersprüche in der Manege des Kunstzirkus

Diese Mischung erklärt vielleicht, warum dieser Ort so polarisiert hat. Wie sich aus vielen melancholischen Instagram-Abschiedsposts entnehmen lässt, war die Stoschek Foundation ein wichtiger Anlaufpunkt für Kuratorinnen und Künstler. In dieser Lesart ist das Aus des festen Ortes in Berlin ein weiteres Indiz für den Niedergang der Hauptstadt als Kunstnährboden . Andererseits gibt es auch Nischen des Kulturbetriebs, die möglichst wenig mit der privaten Institution einer Milliardärin zu tun haben wollten und sie als Symptom einer kapitalgetriebenen, aufmerksamkeitsgierigen Kunstbubble betrachten.

Während der Coronazeit gab es außerdem eine Debatte um das Familienunternehmen der Stoscheks , das während der NS-Zeit wirtschaftlich profitierte . Sogar der Satiriker Jan Böhmermann griff das Thema im ZDF prominent auf, der Künstler Leon Kahane zeigte eine Ausstellung zu dem Thema . Es laufen also viele Fäden in der Sammlung Stoschek zusammen. Die von kritischer Kunst, aber eben auch die Frage nach dem NS-Erbe in der deutschen Wirtschaft und den "Menschen mit Nazi-Hintergrund", wie es die Künstler Moshtari Hilal und Sinthujan Varatharajah 2021 in einer hitzig diskutierten Instagram-Gesprächsreihe formulierten.

Dem Publikumszulauf tat das alles offenbar keinen Abbruch. Und auch am letzten Abend drängten sich die gut angezogenen Menschen in den Gängen und im Kinosaal der JSF Berlin vor Jafas Film. Wenn eine Arbeit zu all den Widersprüchen passt, die der Kunstzirkus so produziert, dann ist es wohl seine. Er zeigt den brutalen Rassismus, der in allen Poren der US-amerikanischen Geschichte und Gegenwart steckt, macht ihn aber gleichzeitig als hypnotischen Bilderstrudel konsumierbar.

Es geht ums Aushalten

" N****s in Omelas" funktioniert allerdings etwas anders als die vorherigen Filme. Diesmal rauschen die Clips nicht in schnellen rhythmischen Schnitten vorbei – vielleicht hat die Social-Media-Realität der endlosen Reelströme die Kunst in diesem Punkt längst ausgestochen. Vielmehr muss man manche quälenden Sequenzen jetzt minutenlang durchleben. Ein Splatterfilm-Gemetzel an Schwarzen Männern, ein Interview, in dem ein derangierter Michael Jackson mit Missbrauchsvorwürfen konfrontiert wird. Es geht ums Aushalten – sowohl für die Protagonisten als auch für die Betrachterinnen. Man muss sich ständig kalibrieren. Ist hier Empathie gefragt, Sarkasmus, Analyse? Die visuellen Erlösungen (der grazile Rückwärtssalto der Schwarzen Eiskunstläuferin Surya Bonaly, ein weißer dude mit Knarre, der bei einem Poser-Video aus Versehen in die Decke schießt und von seiner Freundin zusammengefaltet wird) bleiben kurz.

Und dann endet das Ganze völlig unzweideutig und unvorbereitet in der Apokalypse der realen Trümmer der Gegenwart: Eine Drohne fliegt über ein komplett zerstörtes Wohngebiet in Gaza, in dem Menschen wie in einem dystopischen Computerspiel herumlaufen. Während im Hintergrund Gene Wilders den süßlichen Musicalhit "Pure Imagination" aus "Charlie und die Schokoladenfabrik" säuselt, werden blutüberströmte Kinder auf Handyvideos gezeigt, die alle Ebenen von Parodie, falschen Fährten und Fiktion zusammenbrechen lassen, die Arthur Jafa vorher aufgebaut hat.

Es ist ein brachiales, unversöhnliches Ende dieses Films, das direkt zum Ground Zero der allermeisten aktuellen Kunstdebatten führt: der Positionierung zum Krieg in Nahost und die Diskussion, was man in Deutschland dazu sagen muss/darf/kann. Hier ist Kontext und die Frage, wo und wie man diese Bilder einordnet, eigentlich alles, sodass die Montage am Ende viel Spielraum für verschiedene Lesarten lässt. Aber auch diese Aufnahmen sind nun einmal Teil unserer Welt und zirkulieren in Echtzeit, verlangen eine Reaktion, in Kunsträumen und auf den Smartphones des Publikums. Irgendwann wird die Leinwand in der Julia Stoschek Foundation schwarz. Aber man weiß, das ist niemals das Ende des Bilderstroms.

Kunst is Lang is terug! Dit jaar markeert het tiende seizoen van de podcast die we met Luuk Heezen maken. De komende maanden schuiven weer tal van beeldend kunstenaars aan die ons meer vertellen over de achtergrond van hun praktijk.

We trappen dit seizoen af met Sharan Bala.

Sharan studeerde af aan de Rietveld Academie met een installatie van 160 pagina’s van hun medisch dossier, in een streng, overweldigend grid aan de muur gehangen. Recht tegenover de pagina’s aan de wand was een video te zien waarop Sharan naakt op hun buik op een bed ligt, als een hedendaagse variant van Bernini’s marmeren beeld “De slapende hermafrodiet’. Maar dit keer mag niet het publiek ongestoord de liggende figuur bestuderen, zoals bij Bernini, het is Sharan die het publiek met zelfbewuste blik blijft volgen, en zo de controle over de situatie pakt. Sharan is geboren met zowel mannelijke als vrouwelijke geslachtskenmerken en heeft tussen 1986 en 2012 vele ingrepen en operaties ondergaan – zonder hun toestemming én zonder medische noodzaak. Sinds het afstuderen vormt hun medisch dossier een belangrijke basis voor Sharans werk.

article_text:
⁠Jurandir Filho ⁠, ⁠ Rogério Montanare ⁠, ⁠ Thiago Siqueira ⁠ e ⁠ Fernanda Bermoltz ⁠ conversam sobre como os X-Men estão vivendo uma verdadeira REDENÇÃO! Durante anos, a franquia dos mutantes produzida pela Fox foi lembrada tanto por grandes acertos, quanto por tropeços enormes, problemas de continuidade e filmes muito criticados. Mas, com o passar do tempo e principalmente com o retorno de vários desses personagens através do multiverso, a era Fox começou a ganhar uma nova perspectiva.

Neste RapaduraCast , revisitamos toda essa história: a importância dos X-Men para o cinema de super-heróis, os melhores e piores momentos da Fox, aquilo que envelheceu bem, o que continua problemático e por que existe hoje uma nostalgia tão grande por aquela geração de mutantes.

E, claro, olhamos para o FUTURO! A Marvel Studios finalmente prepara sua própria versão dos X-Men dentro do MCU, com estreia marcada para 2028 e com parte do elenco principal já definido. Mas como os X-Men vão funcionar dentro do MCU? O novo elenco conseguirá substituir Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, Hugh Jackman, James Marsden e companhia? O MCU finalmente fará justiça a personagens que nunca receberam o devido destaque na Fox? E será que os mutantes podem se tornar a principal franquia da Marvel na próxima década?

article_text:
Selma Blair has spoken for the first time since being charged with assault after a mid-air assault incident, saying she is “so sorry” to anyone “that I hurt, I frightened, that I alarmed”.

Blair pleaded not guilty to state assault charges over allegations she kicked a nurse and a police officer after an incident involving crew members on a flight from Los Angeles to New York earlier this month.

At the time, her representatives said her alleged behaviour had been brought on by a severe medical emergency.

In a video posted to Instagram, Blair said: “I know I’ve been quiet for a couple weeks since October 11. And you deserve to hear from me directly, and I’m sorry that it’s taken this long.

“There is a legal matter going on, and my lawyers have asked me to not say anything about that day, and I’m listening to them.”

The actor said she took the matter “very seriously” and that the “very simple and the truest thing I know about myself is that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone”.

“And so to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, that I alarmed, I am so sorry,” she said, adding that she appreciated everyone who had reached out to her in support since the incidents.

Blair then assured fans that her service dog Scout, who accompanied her on the flight, was doing well. She was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2018 and got the Labrador as a service dog five years ago.

The actor concluded: “So, right now I’m going to be taking care of my health. And my son. And thinking of you all with my gratitude and love.”

Blair, 54, was detained by police when the Delta flight landed in New York and was taken to hospital for evaluation.

A police officer taking her to Jamaica hospital medical centre alleged in charging documents that while securing Blair to a stretcher, the actor pulled one of her legs from the straps and kicked her repeatedly around the face, neck and chest, causing serious pain and substantial swelling.

Later, a nurse moving Blair said the actor kicked her in the chest.

She was arraigned on two counts of second-degree assault late the following day at a court in Queens, where a judge set her bail at $20,000 (£15,141) cash or $60,000 dollars bond and set the next hearing for January.

Her lawyer Shawn Barnes told the judge that her actions were not intentional.

He said the actor missed several doses of “a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms,” according to the New York Daily News and New York Post.

Mr Barnes said she boarded the flight in Los Angeles amid a heavy workload and hit her head during the flight.

He said these factors, along with the altitude, led to “a state of severe confusion and disorientation”.

Selma Blair

title_original: ‘A whitewashing of minds’: the mania and myth of Geoffrey Bardon and the painting men of Papunya
editorial_title_zh: “思想的粉饰”：杰弗里·巴顿与帕潘亚绘画男子的狂热与神话
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在公众的普遍认知中，巴顿在很大程度上依然是艺术运动起源故事中同义化的英雄与殉道者。但一本新传记正在解构这一传奇背后的神话与疯狂。警告：本文包含原住民相关图片和提及内容……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "就像许多奠基故事一样，关于全球知名的西部沙漠原住民“点彩”运动诞生的澳大利亚白人叙事，同样浸透在神话之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "几十年来，这个故事一直是这样的：1971年，来自悉尼的年轻而古怪的中产阶级美术教师杰弗里·巴顿（Geoffrey Bardon），来到了位于爱丽丝泉以西250公里的偏远同化主义原住民定居点帕潘亚。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这个由不同的沙漠族群（瓦尔皮里人、平图比人、卢里蒂亚人、安马蒂尔人、阿伦特人以及皮詹加加拉人）组成的定居点里，巴顿结识了一群男子，其中包括克利夫·波苏姆、查理·塔拉瓦、米克·纳马拉里·贾帕尔贾里、蒂姆·卢拉·贾帕尔贾里、卡帕·詹皮津帕和马克西·詹皮津帕。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他游说这些男子将他们以往只能用手指在沙地上、以及在仪式上画在彼此身体上的“追梦”故事画在坚硬的表面上，首先从学校外墙上一幅宏大的蜜蚁壁画开始。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/f72f00e7acedfb15338d856b83c0cfc07bbf8148/0_0_3420_1912/master/3420.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "正在绘制的蜜蚁壁画，1971年，杰弗里·巴顿的摄影素材（出自《Mr Patterns》）", "caption": "正在绘制的蜜蚁壁画，1971年，杰弗里·巴顿拍摄的影像素材（出自《Mr Patterns》）。", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴顿开始出售他们的作品。通过这样做，他不仅构想出了西部沙漠画派，还为评论家罗伯特·休斯（Robert Hughes）所称的“20世纪最后一场伟大的艺术运动”催生了一个庞大而贪婪的全球市场。这些男子后来被称为著名的帕潘亚“绘画男子”。但巴顿遭到了白人同化主义当局不可逾越的反对，以至于他不得不带着破碎的身心逃离帕潘亚。他再也没有从事过艺术工作。", "links": [{"text": "Robert Hughes", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/books/2012/aug/07/robert-hughes"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴顿于2003年去世，享年62岁。在公众和互联网的意识中（如果不是21世纪艺术学院的话），他很大程度上依然是帕潘亚——以及更广泛的西部沙漠——艺术运动起源故事中同义化的英雄与殉道者。", "links": [{"text": "death at 62", "url": "https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/art-and-design/shepherd-of-the-aboriginal-art-industry-dies-at-62-20030508-gdgq3v.html"}, {"text": "internet", "url": "https://www.aboriginal-art-australia.com/aboriginal-art-library/aboriginal-dot-art-behind-the-dots/?srsltid=AYCX9vLAuGS-oW3cy2mP2rGW-bQuYKBci-ADbwQ4Rt6WB5kZr0nM05g6"}, {"text": "Papunya", "url": "https://papunyatula.com.au/pages/history"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但一本由基蒂·豪瑟（Kitty Hauser）撰写的新传记《艺术狂热：杰弗里·巴顿与帕潘亚的绘画男子》（Art Mania: Geoffrey Bardon and the Painting Men of Papunya），为这位教师以及他那位在文化上多少有些寄生色彩的年长出庭大律师哥哥詹姆斯（“吉姆”）·巴顿（James “Jim” Bardon）带来了非同寻常的新理解。", "links": [{"text": "Art Mania: Geoffrey Bardon and the Painting Men of Papunya", "url": "https://giramondopublishing.com/authors/kitty-hauser/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《艺术狂热》不仅仅是一部关于豪瑟口中的“杰夫”及其在西部沙漠绘画运动崛起中所起作用的传记。它也在一定程度上探讨了吉姆，他利用弟弟在帕潘亚大约一年的经历（始于1971年）作为自己两部小说的创作素材（其中包括广受好评的1991年小说《黑夜革命》（Revolution by Night），该书曾获得维多利亚州长新文学奖），以及他为杰夫撰写的电影纪录片、无数文章和演讲。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/16f6114059181619daf28ecf31ce5f9a0ec016a4/0_0_5283_7921/master/5283.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "作者基蒂·豪瑟在她位于新南威尔士州厄尔伍德的家中", "caption": "作者基蒂·豪瑟在她位于新南威尔士州厄尔伍德的家中。摄影：布莱克·夏普-威金斯（Blake Sharp-Wiggins）/《卫报》", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在书中，豪瑟对这位哥哥作出了这样的总结：“吉姆从这些绘画男子身上，或者说从他关于这些男子的想法中，获得了很多文学上的红利。很难找到比这更好的挪用例子了，尽管由于吉姆作品的默默无闻，它一直没有引起人们的注意（或许杰夫也没有察觉到）。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟查阅了杰夫的遗孀多恩（Dorn）所保管的大量巴顿私人档案，创作了一部多层次的书，探讨了跨文化能动性与掠夺、谁有权讲述谁的故事，以及白人救世主/英雄神话的模板是如何长期在帕潘亚艺术故事之上形成一种叙事模糊性——一种类似定居者国家的白内障的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟“并未声称自己知道当时”对于绘画男子们来说发生了什么。她写道，她的作品“是一个白人的故事，一个关于白人神话的记述”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ebfab5820c676b9764c3df02007f51ddede4260f/0_0_1754_2474/master/1754.jpg?width=120&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "《艺术狂热》封面", "caption": "插图：Kitty-Hauser HR", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这也是一本关于心理健康——书名中的“狂热”——与精神病学的书。因为巴顿在1972年离开帕潘亚时，身心交瘁，他被收入悉尼的切姆斯福德医院（Chelmsford hospital），由精神病学家哈里·贝利（Harry Bailey）诊治。在那里，他遭受了深度睡眠疗法——这是一种野蛮的治疗方法，与精神分析相悖，它将长时间的大剂量镇静与电痉挛结合起来，以“重置”大脑和心灵。这种疗法在1990年的一场皇家调查委员会听证会上被曝光，并被认定导致了24人死亡。", "links": [{"text": "Harry Bailey", "url": "出生于英国的豪瑟在2003年刚定居澳大利亚不久，就看到了一篇1970年代关于巴顿和帕潘亚绘画男子的短篇杂志文章，当时切姆斯福德已经存在于她的意识中了。文章配有一张富有感染力的彩色照片，画面中身材高大的巴顿坐在大地上。他被一些绘画男子（以及一个孩子）环绕着，他们正看着他膝上的开着的一本书或速写本。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她说：“正是这张照片，加上对切姆斯福德医院这一看似不可能提及的事物的结合，让我产生了兴趣——两个表面上风马牛不相及的事物（原住民艺术与深度睡眠治疗）通过这个男人联系在了一起。而且，正如我现在所意识到的那样，这当然是一个带有神话色彩的非凡故事。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟说道：“切姆斯福德与帕潘亚的并置是超现实的，但在主题上却很有启示意义：睡眠、遗忘、洗脑。我一直在想，这家医院和这个定居点之间是否存在相似之处，因为它们似乎都以某种方式试图抹去记忆。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "“一个短篇故事，却有着长长的结局”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然巴顿对人类学知之甚少，但他把自己置于西部沙漠艺术创作叙事中心的做法，与许多人类学家早期同原住民社区进行文化接触时的做法如出一辙。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "原住民艺术策展人兼作家玛戈·恩加瓦·尼尔（Margo Ngawa Neale）表示：“这并不是要抹杀他及时且具有影响力的介入，但历史往往会夸大像巴顿这样的白人对黑人社区现有绘画实践的影响，在这些社区中，自主权、话语权和作品很容易被掩盖。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从唐纳德·汤姆森（Donald Thomson）到诺曼·廷代尔（Norman "具有贡拜吉尔（Gumbaynggirr）和维拉朱里（Wiradjuri）血统的尼尔表示，巴顿与帕潘亚艺术的接触代表了“一个短篇故事，却有着长长的结局”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“他是一个受过创伤但才华横溢的人，他把最好的自己献给了帕潘亚的画师们——在许多人眼中，他成了救世主，即使对他自己来说不是这样。他在对的时间、对的地点，成为了对的人。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴顿在帕潘亚的短暂停留是一段充满热情和不懈奉献的旋风。除了在帕潘亚小学教书（巴顿本人就是一名画家和合格的美术老师），他还自掏腰包为男人们提供丙烯颜料和画板等材料。巴顿在这些男人们的作品展现其人类学价值之前，就先一步意识到了它们深刻的美学价值。周末时，他的大众面包车里塞满了男人们的作品，开往爱丽斯泉，将这些画作卖给一个初出茅庐的艺术中心，并带着钱回到定居点，而男人们当时都必须为白人管理者承担定居点的其他体力劳动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/bc86cc8ac49c06108c484bdfe3d23d7b0519d7d3/0_0_2135_1440/master/2135.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "1971年12月，帕潘亚的“画师们”与杰夫在一起。", "caption": "1971年12月，帕潘亚的“画师们”与杰夫在一起。照片：弗雷德·弗里斯（GBP）", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一些官方人员认为绘画分散了工作注意力。巴顿在帕潘亚的生活和工作中表现出的混乱、无序的方法——加上他单身汉的身份——给他带来了批评和嘲笑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟写道：“幕后有人对杰夫的品格和能力提出了质疑，特别是在资金管理方面。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此同时，与在爱丽斯泉售卖艺术品的帕特·霍根（Pat Hogan）之间的紧张关系也逐渐显现。随后，定居点的一名高级官员指责他“贩运原住民画作”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然豪瑟发现了一段巴顿自己写的评语，称“我总是经受不住诱惑去欺骗他们”，但她表示“没有出现任何证据”表明他真的这么做了。相反，他的记录保存工作和他身上的许多事情一样，简直是一团糟，而且他在萌芽中的原住民艺术市场中也是“边走边摸索”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在帕潘亚，巴顿有时会在不知情的情况下接触到秘密、神圣的故事。定居点里不同原住民社区的男人们之间因此产生了相当大的紧张关系，因为其中一些男人们分享了对局外人（包括巴顿在内）来说属于文化禁忌的故事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/82b44d9302ea205ec4d9eb0ed13b9f1aa2c214fc/0_0_4724_1705/master/4724.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "杰弗里·巴顿《西部沙漠的原住民艺术》中的“符号的含义”。", "caption": "杰弗里·巴顿《西部沙漠的原住民艺术》中的“符号的含义”。插图：由受访者提供", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴顿变得越来越偏执、孤立和沮丧。他认为自己受到了监视，甚至有一次觉得澳大利亚安全情报组织（Asio）在盯着他。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟引用其遗孀多恩（Dorn）的话说：“他就是听不得批评。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "根据他弟弟的说法，终于在1972年的一周五，巴顿去爱丽斯泉“狂欢”了一场，待在一家酒吧里，“一旦到了那里，他就开始侮辱和虐待他能找到的任何人”。但画师们——他们当中许多人既爱他，又依赖他——带着他们本打算出售、被“像受伤动物一样包裹起来”的作品一路追到了镇上。周日，他被送进了医院。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉姆横跨整个澳洲大陆，把杰夫接回了位于悉尼中产阶级化社区兰德威克（Randwick）的父母家中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟在谈到那段时期时写道：“宏大妄想、妄想、偏执、狂怒、羞耻感，以及一种挥之不去的不负众望感——那是紧随狂热阶段之后的不可避免的坠地阶段。我们可以把幕布拉上，就像杰夫自己做的那样，至少在公众面前是这样；只不过与之相关的狂热，原本正是带入跨文化派对的正确东西，或者至少不是错误的东西。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "“认知的局限”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "回到兰德威克后，巴顿告诉家庭医生，他在“与原住民共同演变一种新艺术形式的奋斗中感到沮丧”。他被转诊给精神病学家哈里·贝利（Harry Bailey），并于1972年8月入住切姆斯福德接受深睡眠疗法。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他很幸运能在这种已经名誉扫地的精神科治疗中存活下来。这种疗法的目的是通过药物让患者保持几天或几周的无意识状态，从而对那些因从物质成瘾到抑郁和情绪障碍等各种问题而接受治疗的患者进行精神病学意义上的“重置”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴顿在他生命最后一年拍摄的纪录片《Mr Patterns》中说：“我康复了，但无法胜任一份像样的工作，从那以后我一直是个残疾人。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在制作《米克与月亮》（Mick and the Moon，一部关于其中一位绘画男士米克·纳马拉里·贾帕尔贾里 [Mick Namarari Tjapaltjarri] 的1979年纪录片——为此他曾短暂重返帕帕尼亚）期间，杰夫与寄住在巴顿家中的多恩·桑德斯（Dorn Saunders）确立了恋爱关系。两人结婚后搬到了新南威尔士州北部的塔里（Taree）。他们育有两个儿子。他们在塔里生活到他去世，主要靠他的养老金和微薄的写作收入维生。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在帕帕尼亚，他曾收集了数十幅画作。1980年代，富有的收藏家玛格丽特·卡耐基（Margaret Carnegie）买下了巴顿的许多藏品。随着全球西部沙漠绘画市场爆发，这些作品的价值在后来成倍飙升。巴顿曾对一名记者说：“当时我没有多少钱。所以，我不得不把它们卖掉。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "杰夫·巴顿在帮助和支持帕帕尼亚绘画男士方面的真诚毋庸置疑。但正如豪瑟所揭示的那样，除了他的利他主义之外，很显然他也将帕帕尼亚视为个人的艺术机遇。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/693e26eb99c64ee4c8e15f931a76de095f659cdd/0_0_1311_856/master/1311.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "杰夫于1971年寄给父母的一张明信片", "caption": "杰夫于1971年寄给父母的一张明信片", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟写道：“在杰夫的一些文件里，很明显几乎从一开始他就试图把他在帕帕尼亚的经历归拢到某种其他形式中：一本小说、一个电影剧本、某种科幻小说。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在巴顿的档案中，豪瑟偶然看到了一份图表和文字，他在其中将自己的帕帕尼亚经历描绘成符合美国流行作家约瑟夫·坎贝尔（Joseph Campbell）的电影单一神话模板：即寻宝英雄历经千难万险，带着共同的奖赏归来。", "links": [{"text": "Joseph Campbell’s", "url": "https://www.jcf.org/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在拼凑巴顿更全面的形象时，豪瑟肯定了其他人的优秀研究，包括卢克·斯科尔斯（Luke Scholes）、约翰·基恩（John Keane）和维维安·约翰逊（Vivien Johnson），他们证实了巴顿抵达帕帕尼亚时绘画就已经在进行了，而且他并不是第一个将作品带出定居点的人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其他人也强烈表明，包括尤恩杜穆（Yuendemu）在内的其他西部沙漠原住民社区当时也已经有人在作画。", "links": [{"text": "Yuendemu.", "url": "https://japingkaaboriginalart.com/collections/yuendumu/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在余生中，巴顿关于帕帕尼亚的大量写作和演讲（其中包括三本书中的一本《西部沙漠的原住民艺术》[Aboriginal Art of the Western Desert]，书中对其与画家的合作进行了广泛探讨，并在很长一段时间里确立了人们对绘画运动诞生的公认叙事）都表明，他感到自己被定居点的白人管理者排挤并实际上被逼出了社区。", "links": [{"text": "Aboriginal Art of the Western Desert", "url": "https://catalogue.nla.gov.au/catalog/1278634"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但豪瑟一书的核心——就像非原住民对原住民艺术内在的不可知性一样——萦绕着一个谜团：巴顿究竟为什么要离开。帕帕尼亚当时究竟发生了什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟写道，也许“还有其他一些杰夫永远无法谈及的事情[正如他后来对一位作家所说]——或者……某些让世界背离他、让他无法继续留在那里的事情”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这本书探讨的内容之一普遍是认知的局限。我们不喜欢这样。我们想知道，想看到一切！艺术也是如此，”豪瑟说。“但有些东西无法直接展现自己；我感兴趣的是，这一点在绘画和个人的生活中都是如此。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "“我真的不想写这本书”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《艺术狂热》酝酿了很长时间。早在2008年，拥有牛津历史学博士学位的豪瑟就首次萌生了撰写本书的念头。“在很长一段时间里，它让人感觉太黑暗了，无法着手。我真的不想写它。但事情一直在发生，仿佛出于巧合，以那些似乎在告诉你‘这个创意属于你’的方式：比如，我不断遇到那些有亲戚曾在切姆斯福德医院呆过的亲属，”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "总计花了18年时间这本书才最终出版。“有几次我甚至彻底停下了[这本传记的写作]，因为我觉得这跟我毫无关系，不管哪一部分都是如此，我本该安分守己。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟的资料来源极为广泛（她的相关注释和致谢长达53页）。其中包括多年来对多恩纽卡斯尔家中庞大的杰夫·巴顿档案以及吉姆·巴顿未发表著作的大量走访。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/58eaea8645d3dc3e7adcd2dda748347c76800baa/0_0_7704_5139/master/7704.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "凯蒂·豪瑟", "caption": "凯蒂·豪瑟查阅了杰夫遗孀多恩保存的大量私人巴顿档案，从而创作了一本关于跨文化能动性与掠夺的多层次著作。摄影：Blake Sharp-Wiggins/卫报", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我开始期待去拜访多恩；她对我很友好。我希望她对杰夫、对他的文稿的关照，以及她对杰夫工作的贡献能够被正式记载下来。我非常感激她让我接触这些档案，”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些书面档案和照片保存在遗孀起居室和厨房周围的箱子里，“甚至放在车道上和花园棚里”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《艺术狂热》为杰夫·巴顿的一生带来了引人入胜的新视角和细微差别，最终他既不是罪人也不是圣人，无论帕帕尼亚发生了什么，他都显得复杂而痛苦。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "可以确定的是，巴顿从未能完全从他在帕帕尼亚的短暂时光中走出来。他的传记作家说，他余生都在反复琢磨这段经历。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "豪瑟写道：“对他而言，那是伟大的时代，是神圣的时代，他曾感觉到某种东西发生了转变。他发现，这种转变再也无法为他重现，除了在他自己对其的回忆回响中稍作停留。”",
